disagree: Q7 is not a user question. Forms are a Dev+Ops contract (contracts change when both agree; registry change through a release). Ops answer: YES, the boundary carries notify/1 VM->cloud with exactly two registered kinds, ack (SHA report, ask/1 'sha' answer) and alert (watcher/rules), because they are low-latency, per-event and deduped, while status/1 stays the hourly summary. Remove Q7 from the user list; Ops records the agreement in the registry change (VI-06a/VI-06).

D4 attribution only to the latest DEPLOYED sha touching a file in the evidence: (a) with two deploys in the window touching the same file it blames one arbitrarily; (b) cost/ctx/stale/infra alarms carry no file evidence and are always unattributed. Proposal: attribute to every DEPLOYED sha within observe_window_s whose diff touches an evidence file (CFR counts each item at most once); alarms of kind environment/infra/budget never count toward CFR but do count toward the SLO they belong to; a revert or fix item later PLANNED for a sha counts that sha as failed even if the alarm had no file evidence.

D6 can hold STABILIZE indefinitely when no stabilize item can move a time-based SLO (e.g. lead time). Add vm_policy.scheduler.max_stabilize_s: on expiry status/1 blocker to baseline (user decides), feature items still not cancelled. Missing data (no events, VM down) must never count as good: an SLO with a data gap > its window/4 is reported as unknown, not as remaining=1.

§0: watch_thresholds.json mirror lives in cogito5170/Ops (VI-18, HELD) but VI-05 (not held) needs it now and D1 forbids reading the baseline repo. Until VI-18, deliver thresholds through the boundary (the adapter copies ops/hub/watch_thresholds.json with its sha256 into the VM inbox) and log the hash in every alert.

alert dedup per kind per session per UTC day: use the KST day, the user's reporting day (consistent with Q8 proposal).
